title: Let's say you HAVE to shoot a film in 60/120fps. What type of film are you making that's best suited for a high frame rate?

commenti.body:
I don't particularly think high framerates are really bad for regular story driven types of films. I do however think regular film making crutches like excessive motion blur which fit and look right with 24-30fps stand out with higher framerates. Likewise with the way panning shots a other film making techniques are handled, in the hfr movies I've seen those just looked kind of weird.

I feel like it would work really well for a dramatic western or period type of film. Focus on long cuts and slower camera motions but allow the characters fast moving actions to be captured correctly for once. Let the environment and weather become a true visual feature in a story, water or wind could feel really visceral through dense movements that would usually be hidden by blurring.

Just my thoughts anyway.
Intense weather and stationary camera was the first thing that came to my mind as well.

Interesting, that's basically the point of the short film [Meridian](https://youtu.be/u1LTx4h7D_0?si=2lcSxVHWi3crcOLE), it's a 4k 60fps film with lots of sunlight and smoke and rain etc to test Netflix's streaming quality.

That video is a really cool example. Yeah definitely giving me LA Noire vibes. 

I was actually thinking after making my comment that something focusing on really fine facial features and brief movements would be a good use of hfr. This really supports that, every muscle movement on their faces is so much more visible than what we see with regular film rates. Even the fairly quick blinking lighting in it seems to function better, less flashing lights and more quickly fading in and out.
LA Noire has been locked to 30 in all versions because how the facial capture was implemented.
